raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Add a `/health/ready` readiness endpoint so orchestrators can tell a live engine apart from one that should receive traffic. `/health` stays the liveness check.

`/health/ready` returns:

- `200` when the engine is idle, or busy and making progress.
- `503` when the engine is dead (`EngineDeadError`).
- `503` when the engine has unfinished requests and has produced no output for `VLLM_READY_CHECK_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S` (default 30 s) since it became busy, or no output for `VLLM_READY_CHECK_PROGRESS_TIMEOUT_S` (default 10 s) after the last output (`EngineUnhealthyError`).
- `503` when the engine core does not answer the readiness check within `VLLM_READY_CHECK_TIMEOUT_S` (default 5 s), e.g. when a forward pass or collective hangs and the busy loop never services the utility call.

Progress means any request output with new tokens, a pooling output, or a finish reason, so pooling/embedding servers under sustained load stay ready. The busy timer starts only when the scheduler goes from idle to busy, so a steady stream of new requests cannot mask a stall. With DP load balancing, every engine is checked and the first unready engine is reported.

## Changes

- `EngineCore.check_ready` plus readiness bookkeeping in `add_request` / `abort_requests` / step outputs.
- `check_ready_async` on the core clients; `DPLBAsyncMPClient` checks all engines.
- `EngineClient.check_ready` / `AsyncLLM.check_ready`, bounded by `VLLM_READY_CHECK_TIMEOUT_S`.
- `EngineUnhealthyError` in `vllm/v1/engine/exceptions.py`.
- `GET /health/ready` route, excluded from Prometheus HTTP metrics like `/health`.
- New env vars: `VLLM_READY_CHECK_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S`, `VLLM_READY_CHECK_PROGRESS_TIMEOUT_S`, `VLLM_READY_CHECK_TIMEOUT_S`.
- Docs and the Helm chart now point readiness probes at `/health/ready`.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/engine/test_async_llm_health.py tests/entrypoints/serve/instrumentator/test_health.py
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
```

## Test Result

Run locally on CPU (pytest with `--noconftest`, since the repo conftest needs an accelerator):

- `tests/v1/engine/test_async_llm_health.py` and `tests/entrypoints/serve/instrumentator/test_health.py`: 20 passed.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` (ruff, mypy, typos, markdownlint, and the other configured hooks): all passed.

GPU end-to-end tests were not run.

AI-assisted (GitHub Copilot, factory-droid, Claude). The submitter reviewed the changes.

## Code Review

This pull request implements a dedicated `/health/ready` endpoint for readiness probes, distinct from the `/health` liveness probe. The implementation includes documentation updates, Helm chart changes, and new logic in the `AsyncLLM` engine to track request progress and detect stalls. Review feedback highlighted critical issues in the readiness check logic, noting that stale progress timestamps could lead to incorrect unhealthy reports after idle periods and that the current timestamp update mechanism might mask engine stalls. Code suggestions were provided to address these issues by properly managing the engine's idle state and request timestamps.

![critical](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/critical.svg)

The current readiness check logic has a critical flaw: it will incorrectly raise an `EngineUnhealthyError` after the engine has been idle for longer than `VLLM_READY_CHECK_PROGRESS_TIMEOUT_S`. 

Because `last_progress_at` is never reset to `0.0` after requests finish, a new request arriving after an idle period will be compared against a stale `last_progress_at` timestamp from the *previous* busy period. If that idle period was longer than 10 seconds, the check will fail immediately upon the arrival of the next request. 

The logic should instead compare `last_progress_at` against `_last_request_at` to determine if we are waiting for the first bit of progress for a new batch of work, and ensure `_last_request_at` is reset when the engine becomes idle.

```suggestion
        if not self.output_processor.has_unfinished_requests():
            self._last_request_at = 0.0
            return

        now = time.monotonic()
        last_progress_at = self._last_progress_at_ref[0]

        # If we haven't seen progress since the engine became busy, 
        # use the idle timeout against the time the first request was admitted.
        if last_progress_at < self._last_request_at:
            if now - self._last_request_at > envs.VLLM_READY_CHECK_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S:
                raise EngineUnhealthyError(
                    "Engine has unfinished requests but has not produced "
                    "initial progress.")
            return

        # Otherwise, check if we've made progress recently.
        if now - last_progress_at > envs.VLLM_READY_CHECK_PROGRESS_TIMEOUT_S:
            raise EngineUnhealthyError(
                "Engine has unfinished requests but has not made recent progress.")
```

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The `_last_request_at` timestamp is currently updated for every request admitted to the engine. If the engine is stalled but continues to receive new requests, this logic will continuously reset the timeout, potentially masking the stall indefinitely. It should only be updated when the engine transitions from an idle to a busy state (or when `_last_request_at` has been reset).

```suggestion
        if self._last_request_at == 0.0:
            self._last_request_at = time.monotonic()
```

Thanks for the review. This was addressed in commit `3967c98b8` (`fix(health): track readiness by busy period`). The readiness tracking was moved into `EngineCore`, where `_busy_since` and `_last_token_at` are reset to `0.0` whenever the engine becomes idle, and `_busy_since` is only set when the engine transitions from idle to busy. This prevents stale timestamps from being used after an idle period.

Thanks for the review. This was addressed in the same commit (`3967c98b8`). `_busy_since` is now only updated when the engine transitions from idle to busy, not on every admitted request, so a stalled engine cannot mask the stall by continuously receiving new requests.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+import asyncio
+import time
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, Mock, patch
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+import vllm.envs as envs
+from vllm.v1.engine import EngineCoreOutput, EngineCoreOutputs, FinishReason
+from vllm.v1.engine.async_llm import AsyncLLM
+from vllm.v1.engine.core import EngineCore
+from vllm.v1.engine.exceptions import EngineDeadError, EngineUnhealthyError
+from vllm.v1.metrics.stats import SchedulerStats
+
+
+class FakeScheduler:
+    def __init__(self, unfinished: bool):
+        self.unfinished = unfinished
+
+    def has_unfinished_requests(self) -> bool:
+        return self.unfinished
+
+    def add_request(self, request) -> None:
+        self.unfinished = True
+
+
+def make_request(request_id: str) -> SimpleNamespace:
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        request_id=request_id,
+        pooling_params=None,
+        kv_transfer_params=None,
+        ec_transfer_params=None,
+        abort_immediately=False,
+    )
+
+
+def make_core(*, unfinished: bool = True) -> EngineCore:
+    core = object.__new__(EngineCore)
+    core.scheduler = FakeScheduler(unfinished)
+    core._busy_since = time.monotonic()
+    core._last_token_at = time.monotonic()
+    return core
+
+
+def make_async_engine(unhealthy_reason: str | None = None) -> AsyncLLM:
+    engine = object.__new__(AsyncLLM)
+    engine.engine_core = SimpleNamespace(
+        check_ready_async=AsyncMock(return_value=unhealthy_reason),
+        shutdown=Mock(),
+    )
+    engine.renderer = None
+    engine.output_handler = None
+    return engine
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_async_llm_check_ready_delegates_to_engine_core():
+    engine = make_async_engine()
+
+    with patch.object(
+        type(engine),
+        "errored",
+        new_callable=lambda: property(lambda self: False),
+    ):
+        await engine.check_ready()
+
+    engine.engine_core.check_ready_async.assert_awaited_once()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_async_llm_check_ready_raises_unhealthy():
+    engine = make_async_engine("not ready")
+
+    with (
+        patch.object(
+            type(engine),
+            "errored",
+            new_callable=lambda: property(lambda self: False),
+        ),
+        pytest.raises(EngineUnhealthyError),
+    ):
+        await engine.check_ready()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_async_llm_check_ready_dead_engine():
+    engine = make_async_engine()
+
+    with (
+        patch.object(
+            type(engine),
+            "errored",
+            new_callable=lambda: property(lambda self: True),
+        ),
+        patch.object(
+            type(engine),
+            "dead_error",
+            new_callable=lambda: property(lambda self: EngineDeadError()),
+        ),
+        pytest.raises(EngineDeadError),
+    ):
+        await engine.check_ready()
+
+    engine.engine_core.check_ready_async.assert_not_awaited()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_async_llm_check_ready_times_out(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch):
+    engine = make_async_engine()
+
+    async def never_returns():
+        await asyncio.Future()
+
+    engine.engine_core.check_ready_async = never_returns
+    monkeypatch.setattr(envs, "VLLM_READY_CHECK_TIMEOUT_S", 0.01)
+
+    with (
+        patch.object(
+            type(engine),
+            "errored",
+            new_callable=lambda: property(lambda self: False),
+        ),
+        pytest.raises(EngineUnhealthyError, match="readiness check"),
+    ):
+        await engine.check_ready()
+
+
+def test_engine_core_check_ready_idle():
+    core = make_core(unfinished=False)
+
+    assert core.check_ready() is None
+
+
+def test_engine_core_check_ready_allows_initial_progress_timeout():
+    core = make_core()
+    core._busy_since = time.monotonic() - envs.VLLM_READY_CHECK_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S + 1
+    core._last_token_at = 0.0
+
+    assert core.check_ready() is None
+
+
+def test_engine_core_check_ready_stalled_before_first_token():
+    core = make_core()
+    core._busy_since = time.monotonic() - envs.VLLM_READY_CHECK_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S - 1
+    core._last_token_at = 0.0
+
+    assert core.check_ready() is not None
+
+
+def test_engine_core_check_ready_stalled_after_token():
+    core = make_core()
+    core._busy_since = time.monotonic() - envs.VLLM_READY_CHECK_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S - 1
+    core._last_token_at = (
+        time.monotonic() - envs.VLLM_READY_CHECK_PROGRESS_TIMEOUT_S - 1
+    )
+
+    assert core.check_ready() is not None
+
+
+def test_engine_core_check_ready_recent_token():
+    core = make_core()
+    core._busy_since = time.monotonic() - envs.VLLM_READY_CHECK_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S - 1
+    core._last_token_at = time.monotonic()
+
+    assert core.check_ready() is None
+
+
+def test_engine_core_add_request_marks_busy_on_idle_transition():
+    core = make_core(unfinished=False)
+    core._busy_since = 0.0
+    core._last_token_at = 0.0
+
+    core.add_request(make_request("first"))
+
+    assert core._busy_since > 0.0
+    assert core.check_ready() is None
+
+
+def test_engine_core_new_requests_do_not_mask_stall():
+    core = make_core(unfinished=False)
+    core.add_request(make_request("first"))
+    stalled_since = time.monotonic() - envs.VLLM_READY_CHECK_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S - 1
+    core._busy_since = stalled_since
+
+    core.add_request(make_request("second"))
+
+    assert core._busy_since == stalled_since
+    assert core.check_ready() is not None
+
+
+def test_engine_core_progress_ignores_scheduler_stats():
+    core = make_core()
+    core._last_token_at = 0.0
+
+    core._track_readiness_progress(
+        {0: EngineCoreOutputs(scheduler_stats=SchedulerStats())}
+    )
+
+    assert core._last_token_at == 0.0
+
+
+def test_engine_core_progress_tracks_generated_tokens():
+    core = make_core()
+    core._last_token_at = 0.0
+
+    core._track_readiness_progress(
+        {0: EngineCoreOutputs(outputs=[EngineCoreOutput("req", [1])])}
+    )
+
+    assert core._last_token_at > 0.0
+
+
+def test_engine_core_progress_tracks_pooling_outputs():
+    core = make_core()
+    core._last_token_at = 0.0
+
+    core._track_readiness_progress(
+        {
+            0: EngineCoreOutputs(
+                outputs=[
+                    EngineCoreOutput(
+                        "req",
+                        [],
+                        pooling_output=torch.zeros(4),
+                        finish_reason=FinishReason.STOP,
+                    )
+                ]
+            )
+        }
+    )
+
+    assert core._last_token_at > 0.0
+
+
+def test_engine_core_progress_tracks_finished_requests():
+    core = make_core()
+    core._last_token_at = 0.0
+
+    core._track_readiness_progress(
+        {
+            0: EngineCoreOutputs(
+                outputs=[EngineCoreOutput("req", [], finish_reason=FinishReason.ABORT)]
+            )
+        }
+    )
+
+    assert core._last_token_at > 0.0
+
+
+def test_engine_core_reset_readiness_when_idle():
+    core = make_core(unfinished=False)
+
+    core._reset_readiness_if_idle()
+
+    assert core._busy_since == 0.0
+    assert core._last_token_at == 0.0

@@ -161,6 +161,11 @@ async def check_health(self) -> None:
         """Raise if unhealthy."""
         ...
 
+    @abstractmethod
+    async def check_ready(self) -> None:
+        """Raise if not ready to serve traffic."""

![critical](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/critical.svg)

The current readiness check logic has a critical flaw: it will incorrectly raise an `EngineUnhealthyError` after the engine has been idle for longer than `VLLM_READY_CHECK_PROGRESS_TIMEOUT_S`. 

Because `last_progress_at` is never reset to `0.0` after requests finish, a new request arriving after an idle period will be compared against a stale `last_progress_at` timestamp from the *previous* busy period. If that idle period was longer than 10 seconds, the check will fail immediately upon the arrival of the next request. 

The logic should instead compare `last_progress_at` against `_last_request_at` to determine if we are waiting for the first bit of progress for a new batch of work, and ensure `_last_request_at` is reset when the engine becomes idle.

```suggestion
        if not self.output_processor.has_unfinished_requests():
            self._last_request_at = 0.0
            return

        now = time.monotonic()
        last_progress_at = self._last_progress_at_ref[0]

        # If we haven't seen progress since the engine became busy, 
        # use the idle timeout against the time the first request was admitted.
        if last_progress_at < self._last_request_at:
            if now - self._last_request_at > envs.VLLM_READY_CHECK_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S:
                raise EngineUnhealthyError(
                    "Engine has unfinished requests but has not produced "
                    "initial progress.")
            return

        # Otherwise, check if we've made progress recently.
        if now - last_progress_at > envs.VLLM_READY_CHECK_PROGRESS_TIMEOUT_S:
            raise EngineUnhealthyError(
                "Engine has unfinished requests but has not made recent progress.")
```

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The `_last_request_at` timestamp is currently updated for every request admitted to the engine. If the engine is stalled but continues to receive new requests, this logic will continuously reset the timeout, potentially masking the stall indefinitely. It should only be updated when the engine transitions from an idle to a busy state (or when `_last_request_at` has been reset).

```suggestion
        if self._last_request_at == 0.0:
            self._last_request_at = time.monotonic()
```

Thanks for the review. This was addressed in commit `3967c98b8` (`fix(health): track readiness by busy period`). The readiness tracking was moved into `EngineCore`, where `_busy_since` and `_last_token_at` are reset to `0.0` whenever the engine becomes idle, and `_busy_since` is only set when the engine transitions from idle to busy. This prevents stale timestamps from being used after an idle period.

Thanks for the review. This was addressed in the same commit (`3967c98b8`). `_busy_since` is now only updated when the engine transitions from idle to busy, not on every admitted request, so a stalled engine cannot mask the stall by continuously receiving new requests.

## Code Review

This pull request implements a dedicated `/health/ready` endpoint for readiness probes, distinct from the `/health` liveness probe. The implementation includes documentation updates, Helm chart changes, and new logic in the `AsyncLLM` engine to track request progress and detect stalls. Review feedback highlighted critical issues in the readiness check logic, noting that stale progress timestamps could lead to incorrect unhealthy reports after idle periods and that the current timestamp update mechanism might mask engine stalls. Code suggestions were provided to address these issues by properly managing the engine's idle state and request timestamps.
